chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Khattab al-Hallal, from A'ala ibn Razin, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O A'ala! Do you know what is the first tree that sprouted upon the surface of the earth?' I said, 'Allah and His Messenger and the son of His Messenger know best.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the Ajwa (date palm). So whatever is pure/selected, it is the Ajwa, and whatever is other than that, it is merely from its resemblances.'

key_terms.الْعَجْوَةُ: the Ajwa (a specific type of date palm)

ai.seo_question: What was the first tree to grow on Earth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the Ajwa date palm as the primordial tree of Earth, establishing its unique ontological status among flora. This narration is often interpreted by Shia scholars as highlighting the spiritual and medicinal superiority of the Ajwa variety, particularly those from Medina, distinguishing the authentic lineage from later cultivars that are merely 'resemblances' (ashbah).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Khattab Al Hallal, from A’ala Bin Razeyn who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘O A’ala! Do you know what is the first tree planted upon the surface of the earth?’ I said, ‘Allahazwj and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww and a sonasws of Hisazwj Rasoolsaww are most knowing’. Heasws said: ‘It is Al-Ajwa. So whatever is pure so it is Al-Ajwa, and whatever was other than that, so rather it is from its resemblances’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn Khattab al-Hallal from al-‘ Ala’ ibn Razin who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O ‘Ala’, do you know what was the first tree that grew on earth?’ I replied, ‘Allah, His Messenger and the child of His Messenger know best. He (the Imam) said, ‘It was al-‘Ajwah. What is pure is al-‘Ajwah (a certain kind of date) and whatever is other than this they are only of the similar one’s.’”
